messages:
Elena M: heads up — p95 latency for private-prod (us-west-2, VPC) jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms around 12:10 UTC. Loadtest reproduces. Only private/vpc tenants on dedicated nodes affected. Any recent infra or runtime changes?
Samir: checking host metrics now. I see a lot of TCP retrans and short-lived connections in the node netstat. Can you paste a failing request id?
Elena M: req id 6d3f4e9a — reproduced with a 8-token prompt, single-stream. Also noticed a bunch of connection resets in the runtime logs.
Noah (oncall): deploy-bot shows a small runtime rollout at 11:58 (kernel-selector tweak). Noted.
Priya K: interesting — we pushed a kernel selection tweak to prefer the new tiled GEMM for long seqs, but added a fast-path check that touches shared VM pages. On low-latency short prompts that check can add ~200us per call, but shouldn't cause network-level retransmits.
Matt O: looking at node dmesg: ```nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet``` and ```nf_conntrack: hash table entries: 65536```. conntrack metrics spiked at the same time as the latency. Also tc qdisc shows high tx-queue drops.
Samir: that explains the retransmits. If conntrack is full we can see SYNs dropped which causes clients to retry and increases end-to-end latency. Any idea why conntrack jumped?
Priya K: runtime batching changed last week — we moved to micro-batching with short connection lifetimes to keep latency low. That increases ephemeral ports churn and conntrack churn. If a noisy neighbor opens many outbound flows through the NAT, it can fill conntrack.
Elena M: but why only private/vpc? Hosted nodes use cloud NAT with managed pools. Private deployment uses node SNAT and iptables MASQUERADE.
Matt O: exactly — our private VPC nodes rely on local conntrack and a limited SNAT ephemeral port range. I also noticed firewall in that VPC had ICMP blocked for fragmentation-needed which can create PMTU blackholes and more retransmits.
Priya K: TL;DR: two compounding factors — increased flow churn from batching heuristic + blocked ICMP causing PMTU blackholes -> retransmits -> conntrack growth -> conntrack table full -> packet drops -> client retries -> high p95.
Noah (oncall): confirmed correlation with PMTU errors in tcpdump. Example from the capture: ```IP frag needed and DF set (mtu 1400)``` followed by lots of retransmits.
Samir: suggested mitigations: 1) temporarily increase nf_conntrack_max, 2) widen SNAT port pool, 3) allow ICMP fragmentation-needed on firewall, 4) rollback or tune batching heuristic to reuse persistent connections and reuse KV-cache affinity.
Priya K: I can push a runtime tweak to prefer connection reuse for sessions < 2s (turn off micro-batches for these short sessions) — that should reduce ephemeral port churn and improve KV-cache hit stability.
Matt O: doing the infra patch now: ```sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144``` and increased SNAT port range on the nodes. Also added a temporary iptables rule to prioritize established flows.
Matt O: firewall change deployed to allow ICMP type 3/code 4 (fragmentation needed). Verified with smoke tests: `ping -M do -s 1400 <client>` shows no PMTU blackhole.
Priya K: runtime patch rolled out to private nodes (canary 10%). Early telemetry shows connection churn down ~70% and KV cache miss rate reduced.
Samir: perf profiler on runtime shows the kernel-selection fast-path check still consumes cycles, but was not the dominant factor here — network churn was. We'll keep the kernel change queued for a smaller micro-optimization rollback if needed.
Elena M: after infra patches + runtime tune, p95 dropped back to ~130ms for the affected tenants.
Noah (oncall): follow-ups: 1) add alert rule for conntrack utilization (warn at 60%, page at 80%), 2) per-VPC SNAT pools to isolate noisy neighbors, 3) add PMTU blackhole detection to infra dashboards, 4) revert kernel-selector fast-path if perf regression persists.
Priya K: will submit a PR to revert the fast VM-touch check and add a config flag to keep persistent-conn behavior for short sessions. Also adding a metric for KV-cache miss rate by session length.
Matt O: opened infra ticket to make nf_conntrack_max persistent via cloud-init and to document required firewall ICMP settings for private deployments.
Elena M: thanks all — marking this thread resolved for now. If anyone sees regressions after full rollout, re-open. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: incident annotated: root cause = PMTU + conntrack exhaustion exacerbated by micro-batching; mitigations = firewall ICMP allow, conntrack max increase, SNAT expansion, runtime batching tweak.
